title: Facilities
structure: The .content block holds four siblings in this order. (1) .subnav — a pill group (navy-100 background, radius 12, padding 5, width fit-content) containing three .subnav-item divs in order: "Maintenance" carrying .active, "Amenities", "Vendors". (2) .kpi-row — a 4-column grid, gap 16, margin-bottom 20, of four .kpi-card divs. Each .kpi-card contains a .k-top wrapper holding a single .kpi-icon square (34px, navy-100, radius 10) with an inline SVG, then a .k-val, then a .k-lbl. Card 1: wrench SVG, "12", "Open tickets". Card 2: clock SVG, "7", "In progress". Card 3: alert-circle SVG, "2", "Overdue". Card 4: line-chart SVG, "3.2 days", "Avg resolution". (3) .filter-row — flex, gap 10, margin-bottom 16, of five .f-chip divs: "All" with .active (navy-600 fill, white text), "Open", "In progress", "Completed", and a fifth chip pushed right by inline style margin-left:auto;background:var(--red-100);color:var(--red-700); reading "2 overdue". (4) <table class="data-table"> — thead single row of seven <th>: Ticket, Location, Priority, Status, Assigned, Age, and an empty seventh th for the action column. tbody holds five <tr>, each with seven <td> in the order: ticket text, location text, a .priority-dot div (modifier .high/.med/.low, containing an empty <i> then the label), a .status-badge div (modifier .progress/.overdue/.submitted/.completed), assignee text, age text, and finally either a .text-link-sm div reading "Open". Rows in order: #1042 (med / In progress), #1041 (high / Overdue), #1039 (high / Submitted), #1037 (low / In progress), #1031 (med / Completed). No empty state, no chart, no form section on this screen.
table_headers: Ticket | Location | Priority | Status | Assigned | Age | (empty 7th header for row actions)
domain_needs: maintenance_ticket.number — displayed as "#1042", "#1041", "#1039", "#1037", "#1031"; the Ticket cell is the derived concatenation number + " — " + title (em-dash separator with spaces)
maintenance_ticket.title — "Gate lighting", "Pool filter fault", "Leaking pipe", "Broken gym equipment", "Barrier arm sensor"

maintenance_ticket.location_label — "Phase 2 · visitor parking", "Community Centre", "Phase 1 · Lot 9", "Club House", "Main Gate"; two of the five compose estate phase + sub-location with a middot separator, three are a bare common-area/amenity name, so the field must store either a free-text label or a (phase_id, area/unit) pair rendered with " · "
maintenance_ticket.priority — enum {High, Medium, Low}; drives .priority-dot modifier .high (red-700 dot) / .med (amber-600 dot) / .low (slate-300 dot) and the visible label "High" / "Medium" / "Low"

maintenance_ticket.status — enum {Submitted, In progress, Overdue, Completed}; drives .status-badge modifier .submitted (navy) / .progress (amber) / .overdue (red) / .completed (green). Note Overdue is shown as a status value in the same column as the lifecycle states, so it is either a stored status or a derived override when due_at < now
maintenance_ticket.assigned_vendor_id — nullable FK to vendor; renders vendor.name or the literal "Unassigned" when null
vendor.name — "Island Electric Services", "AquaTech Pool Services", "FitFix Equipment Repair", "Gate2_Contractor Ltd" (note the underscore in "Gate2_Contractor Ltd" is verbatim)
maintenance_ticket.submitted_at — the Age column is DERIVED from now − submitted_at and humanised to the largest unit: "2 days", "6 days", "4 hours", "3 days"
maintenance_ticket.closed_at — for a Completed ticket the Age cell is replaced by "Closed Sep 2" (literal "Closed " + closed_at formatted "MMM D", no year)
maintenance_ticket list default sort — descending by ticket number: 1042, 1041, 1039, 1037, 1031 (numbers are non-contiguous, so ids are estate-wide sequential with gaps)
kpi.open_tickets = 12 — DERIVED count of tickets whose status is not Completed (larger than the 5 rows drawn, so the table is paginated or filtered)
kpi.in_progress = 7 — DERIVED count of tickets with status = In progress
kpi.overdue = 2 — DERIVED count of tickets with status = Overdue; the same figure is re-rendered in the right-hand red filter chip as "2 overdue"
kpi.avg_resolution = "3.2 days" — DERIVED mean of (closed_at − submitted_at) across completed tickets, formatted to one decimal place plus the unit word "days"
ticket_filter.status — chip set {All, Open, In progress, Completed} with All as the default active chip; note the chip label is "Open" while the stored status value is "Submitted"
maintenance_ticket.category — not shown on this list but required by screen 18 ("Category: Electrical")
facilities_module.subnav — three tabs {Maintenance, Amenities, Vendors} with Maintenance active at this route
work_order.create — the topbar primary action "New work order" implies a create route for tickets raised by the manager rather than a resident
